title: Dirac's theorem and the switch geometry of perfect matchings
summary: Let $G$ be a graph on an even number $n$ of vertices and let ${\cal M}_G$ be the collection of perfect matchings in $G$. Dirac's theorem says that if the minimum degree $δ(G)$ of $G$ is at least $n/2$, then ${\cal M}_G$ is guaranteed to be non-empty, while this is not necessarily the case if $δ(G) \le n/2-1$. Given an integer $k\ge 2$, let $\mathcal H_k(G)$ be the reconfiguration graph formed on ${\cal M}_G$ by connecting two distinct $M_1,M_2\in {\cal M}_G$ by an edge in $\mathcal H_k(G)$ if $M_1$ can be obtained from $M_2$ by switching at most $k$ edges.
